_comment: Chroma SINGLE-GPU offload LoRA fine-tune. See chroma/train.py. The whole 8.9B model is diced into one chunk per block (59 chunks: embed + 19 double + 38 single + head) and streams from pinned CPU RAM through a small GPU window; the frozen T5-XXL encoder streams the same way. Needs ~22 GB host RAM for the bf16 masters + grad accumulators + AdamW state on the LoRA params.
_comment_topology: parallelism: 'offload' = 1 GPU with weight streaming, 'pipeline' = N GPUs resident, 'pipeline-offload' = N GPUs with streaming. Independent of 'mode' (lora/full), which is the fine-tuning target. devices defaults to cuda:0 for offload.
_comment_chunks: blocks_per_chunk: transformer blocks per streamed chunk (1 = finest; doubles and singles never share a chunk). offload_window: GPU slots streamed ahead (>=2 overlaps load with compute). offload_pin: chunks kept permanently resident. offload_backward: 'checkpoint' (per-chunk recompute, dropout-safe, cheapest VRAM) or 'keep' (fastest, holds every chunk's graph). offload_grad_accum: where microbatch gradients accumulate — 'cpu' for LoRA (small trainable slice, host adds are cheap), 'stream' for full FT. enc_layers_per_chunk: T5-XXL layers per encoder chunk (24 layers; 4 -> 6 chunks of ~680M).
_comment_batch: batch_size is PER MICROBATCH; effective batch = batch_size * n_microbatches.
_comment_timeshift: Chroma uses a resolution-aware shifted logit-uniform schedule. mu = ln(alpha) where alpha is BFL's shift parameter, interpolated between (256px, 0.5) and (1024px, 1.15) in image-token count. Keep y1/y2 at the pretrained values so timesteps stay in-distribution.
_comment_attn: attn_padding: number of T5 padding tokens after each caption left attendable (flow's modify_mask_to_attend_padding).
_comment_eval: eval_interval: steps between preview grids (0 disables previews; each preview streams the whole model once per CFG branch per sampler step).
_comment_ckpt: Path to the Chroma base weights (safetensors, native flow keys). See checkpoints/README.md — downloaded from lodestones/Chroma1-HD.
_comment_mode: mode='lora' (default): LoRA adapters on all nn.Linear + unfrozen RMSNorm scales, whole model bf16 (halves PCIe traffic vs fp32). mode='full': fp32 masters + bf16 autocast compute — see train_offload_full.json for the host-RAM budget. In full mode, resume priority: full_checkpoint > lora_checkpoint (merged into chroma_checkpoint) > chroma_checkpoint.
